name: a2uiverse-composition
description: The A2UIVerse composition extension (SPEC §14): the A2A metadata contract for cross-agent UI composition, internal to the platform (orchestrator ↔ client). Two halves: the composition stamp (provenance, role, generations) on every relayed event, and the synthesis payload — the derived data model of formula leaves and the sort declarations of a merged view — on the event that paints a synthesis surface. Nothing a2uiverse-specific rides the vendor wire. Normative for every language projection; each projection's contract test asserts against this file.

surfaceIdNamespacing.rule: The orchestrator namespaces surfaceId on the four A2UI server→client message types and reverses it on inbound client actions. Component ids, binding paths, and catalog ids are never rewritten.

compositionStamp.carriedOn: every relayed A2A event's metadata, keyed by stampKey

fields.source: Provenance and placement: the app id the event came from. A fragment's surface fills the layout's Slot whose source is this id.
fields.role: Which surface the canvas renders as the composition root: 'shell' | 'fragment'.
fields.vendorContextId: Debug only, gated by orchestrator config.
fields.vendorTaskId: Debug only, gated by orchestrator config.
fields.generations: Per-partition generation counters, keyed by namespaced surfaceId, for every surface this event touched. An integer that only goes up: bumped when an array a live ref indexes into is mutated in place (SPEC §6.2). Absent on the shell's own events — the synthesis surface is derived, not a source.

synthesizeDataModel.carriedOn: metadata.a2uiverseSynthesis of the event that paints a synthesis surface; the tree is painted as ordinary A2UI on the same event
synthesizeDataModel.authors: The orchestrator's Synthesizer writes the merged view; the orchestrator validates it, paints its tree in the shell catalog, and sends the derived data model and the sorts as the synthesis payload.

synthesis.title: SynthesisPayload
synthesis.description: Client-facing: the synthesis branch minus the tree (painted as A2UI) and the note (journaled). Evaluated client-side into the synthesis surface's data model.

ref.description: A cross-partition qualified ref: a pointer that resolves in another surface's data model.

surface.description: The namespaced surfaceId (<appId>:<surfaceId>) the pointer resolves in.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into that surface's data model, where a segment may carry a predicate: `items[sku="x"]` selects the element of `items` whose field `sku` equals the JSON literal "x", and `items[a="x",b=2]` conjoins several field tests until exactly one element matches. Elements are selected by key, never by position: a positional segment into an array does not resolve. A ref is valid while its keys resolve; none matching and several matching are both absent. The value is a JSON literal compared by JSON equality.

formula.description: A leaf of the derived model: one operator over N refs, N ≥ 0. A plain vendor value is a one-argument pass-through. A formula with no refs is a value no source contributes to — absent by construction. Operators are names the shell catalog declares as functions; the contract does not enumerate them. Recognized by shape: an object with exactly `op` and `args` is a formula.

op.description: A function name declared by the shell catalog.

node.description: A node of the free-form derived model: a formula leaf, an object whose values are nodes, or an array of nodes. A scalar anywhere is a violation — every leaf is a formula, never a literal value.

dataModel.description: The derived data model the tree binds to: a JSON shape of the Synthesizer's choosing whose every leaf is a formula. Evaluated client-side into plain values with contributor state at the same paths. The root key `sorts` is reserved: the runtime writes each sort declaration, with the user's current choice, at `/sorts/N` of the synthesis surface's data model, and the tree binds SortControl there.

sort.description: A sort declaration over one array of the derived model. The model names the array, the sortable keys and their labels, and the initial choice; the runtime sorts and keeps the user's choice of key or direction.

path.description: JSON Pointer to the sorted array in the derived model.

options.description: The keys the user may sort by, each with its user-facing label.

key.description: JSON Pointer inside each element of the array, to a formula leaf.
The initial key; one of the options.
